mathematics.assertion_tested: After seeing sudden-source formation failure, test prescribed smooth source assembly with unchanged effective action and 10% target tolerance. Count all source work.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: float64, radial finite volume with energy-adjoint gradient/divergence, velocity Verlet
mathematics.conventions: Same radial source, kernel and units as spherical test; rho(t)=S(t)*rho_final, S=3u^2-2u^3 for u=t/T in [0,1], then 1. Prescribed assembly, NOT derived baryon dynamics. Work=int Sdot*int rho_final Phi r^2 dr dt.

criteria.formation: RMS fractional force error <=0.10 and force nonnegative at every sample during last 80 time units of each run

controls: No drag or changed response coefficients
non_claims: Fixed baryons, not coupled galaxy formation
No independent cold mass, metric/lensing or cosmology
No physical time unit or derived response coefficients
Finite-time approximate agreement is not an attractor theorem
A successful selected assembly history is not a universal attractor or explanation of that assembly timescale.
